title: Freedom of the Dumb
subtitle: A song that is not allowed used to be sung here.

trails.title: The Puppy You know
trails.description: A wet greyhound with a moist tip of nose.

content.text:
The warm fur, the little feet,
The orange color under the light spots, and the pure white yarn.
The unbreakable neck ring that symbolizes loyalty,
And a sincere heart that deserves no suspicion.

Softly, mildly, without resistance,
It licks the white marble.
The frogs, the pebbles, and the stinky socks in the attic forgotten,
It climbs up the cliff like a pious believer,
Poking into the untrackable breeze
At the closest place.

Between the gaps of the stone gate
Are the moist nose and eyes
That you couldn't bear to face.

items.text: Freedom of the Dumb
Two weeks later
Today is the day of the Parade Ceremony.
Junior students walk in pairs, carrying their little stools and heading to the square.
The student performers line up on the stage. Some palms within those white gloves have even become slightly sweaty out of anxiety.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: You weren't in the dormitory last night.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Were you on duty yesterday?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Yes, as I am today.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: I know you are planning something behind the instructors' backs. Please do not act against any regulation stipulated in the Student Handbook.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Otherwise, I'm obliged to report this to the instructor as the monitor student on duty.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... Okay.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Doves are hovering above the square.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: The principal walks onto the stage from the side stair—this can be clearly seen from the stage.

items.speaker: “The Ring”
items.text: Are we ready?

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Yes.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: We got this ...!

items.speaker: Student B
items.text: Let's do this!

items.speaker: Student B
items.text: Good luck to us all!!
The whispering words of encouragement go from one to another and go on.

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: Today, I am honored to be accompanied by the young representative of the St. Pavlov Foundation Committee, Ms. Z;

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: the principal of our close partner, Mr. Claude Smith of Zeno Academy; and the outstanding alumni who graduated last year—

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: to our annual Parade Ceremony!

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: The Parade Ceremony where we show our best image and morale once a year. Each year, the best students would be selected to take a three-month intense training, and become the honor guard of our school and present the fabulous demeanor of our students.

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: And now everyone, the first part of the ceremony—school song.

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: "Peace Lives On."
Looking down the stage, many people sit in lines like those pegs on the pipe organ.
Isabella is the leading singer. Her voice is trembling.

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Nor happiness, nor harmony, nor fame, nor pride, nor strength, nor skill in arms or arts ... ♪

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Shepherd those herds whom blindness makes tame ... ♪

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: What ... what are you singing ...?

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Sonetto is in shock. Mesmer Jr. skips her lyrics and keeps singing in her tender voice.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The voice is thin and hesitant at first, but it later becomes gentler, stronger, and brighter.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: And the principal sitting under the stage finally understands what they are singing.

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: What ... what are they singing?!

items.speaker: Music Instructor
items.text: Mister, Mister! They are singing that poem ... the one on the back of the pamphlet ...!

items.speaker: Music Instructor
items.text: She almost loses her beautiful voice in shock. She sounds tongue-tied.

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: Stop! You stop right now!

items.speaker: Music Instructor
items.text: Sopranos and tenors, stop right now! I forbid you to sing along!

items.speaker: Instructor
items.text: Sonetto! Stop them!

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: The song that should not have existed comes out from all around.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: From the front, the back, her left, and her right. The sound of the unfamiliar lyrics engulfs her like an inescapable trap.

items.speaker: Sonetto
items.text: Sonetto has never felt her heart beating so fast. She becomes dizzy because of this.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Sir, please, listen to us.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Please, give us a chance. Let us be ... let us be ourselves.
The principal's face becomes pale. He turns to the security guard on the side.

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: Get the girl on the right off the stage. NOW!!

items.speaker: Guard
items.text: Copy that.

items.speaker: Safety Supervisor
items.text: Move! Get the water pipe attached on the tap and prepare for the Dumbitter Potion!

items.speaker: Safety Supervisor
items.text: Splash!!

items.speaker: Isabella
items.text: Um ...! Let, let go of me!
More security guards run onto the stage from the side stairs. Isabella, standing on the fringes of the crowd, has been taken down by the guards with their batons.
They can barely open their eyes in the spraying potion.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: ... Isabella!!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Isabella looks at her. This tiny girl gives her a sad smile while being pushed and pulled around by the guards by her side.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Protect Isabella!!
Behind them, more and more people join in the singsing.
The bewildered and helpless children have finally come to realize the adults don't see the world as they do.
They only have each other in this.
With fear, anger, and the feeling of being deprived of the rights to know anything about the outside world for 12 years.
Against the potion, they sing with crying voices and refuse to stop.

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Step back! Step back! Protect yourself. Don't get hurt!

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Listen, stand in circle, hand in hand! Short guys inside!

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: Bloody, it doesn't stop! I just want them to shut up! Is the tear gas in position? Shoot it above them!

items.speaker: Safety Supervisor
items.text: Tear gas is here ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Watch out for the guard batons. Don't get hur ...

items.speaker: Vertin
items.text: Pap!

items.speaker: Principal
items.text: I said shoot it ABOVE them! Why did you shoot it AT them?!

items.speaker: Safety Supervisor
items.text: It, it, it slipped in my hand ...

items.speaker: Safety Supervisor
items.text: This is a song with a surprising opening and a forbidden ending.

items.speaker: Safety Supervisor
items.text: The end of the farce.
TO BE CONTINUED…
